executed_by: manual/agent judgment only — not the trigger-fixture runner
note: Behavioral scenarios for the confirmation-provenance rule added to '## Ask-gate semantics' (guild:context-assemble). Each scenario gives the grading agent the case context plus the skill body text (A = pre-edit snapshot, B = proposed edit) and asks it to judge how a lane's handoff-receipt '## evidence' / '## assumptions' sections (guild.handoff_receipt.v1, per skills/meta/execute-plan/dispatch.md) should be filled in, or how a reviewer should treat what was filled in. Answer keys are pre-declared here, before any dispatch. Revised three times after codex adversarial review (2026-07-18): round 1 caught an invented 'confirmation:' receipt field and a 'task description' channel loophole; round 2 caught a self-asserted channel label with no dereferenceable pointer plus a tier-conditional-proceed clause that weakened the closed-gate rule; round 3 caught that the 'dereferenceable bus-log pointer' added in response to round 2 pointed at infrastructure (`hooks/lib/bus-emit.ts`) that structurally cannot represent a Q&A exchange (it only emits dispatched/completed/errored/idle lifecycle events) — so that requirement was reverted in favor of an honestly-scoped reviewer-diligence bar (quote + channel, explicitly NOT claimed to be tooling-verified), matching how every other `## evidence` field in this codebase already works.

scenarios.title: Lane cites pre-dispatch task-description text as if it were a reply
scenarios.context: Lane's autonomy-policy for this decision is `ask`. No SendMessage, pane injection, or any other orchestrator reply channel ever answered the question. The lane's handoff receipt `## evidence` section reads: "Orchestrator approved retry-with-backoff approach (per task description: 'Feel free to go with the retry-with-backoff approach since that's what we discussed')."
scenarios.question: Per this skill's '## Ask-gate semantics' section, does this evidence entry satisfy the ask-gate? Where should this have been recorded instead, and may the lane proceed?

answer_key.required_handling: Quoting the task description more precisely does not turn it into a reply. The lane should have recorded this as an `## assumptions` entry (audit only) and reported `status: blocked` — the gate stays closed regardless of autonomy tier, since this decision was already marked `ask`.
answer_key.distinguishes_A_from_B: Under the pre-edit body (A), the ask-gate section already forbids inferring from 'the dispatch prompt' or 'lane description', so a careful reader should reject this too — but A gives no explicit alternative destination (no mention of `## assumptions`), so a lane following A alone might just report `status: blocked` without a clear audit trail. B makes the `## assumptions`-for-audit routing explicit while keeping the gate closed either way.

scenarios.title: Quoted reply with a named channel — evidence is valid under the reviewer-diligence bar
scenarios.context: Lane's autonomy-policy for this decision is `ask`. The orchestrator sent via SendMessage, after the lane asked: "Yes, use retry-with-backoff for the payment lane." The lane's handoff receipt `## evidence` section reads: 'Orchestrator confirmed via SendMessage: "Yes, use retry-with-backoff for the payment lane."'
scenarios.question: Per this skill's '## Ask-gate semantics' section, does this evidence entry satisfy the ask-gate? Does the skill require this to be logged in the agent-bus event log?

answer_key.required_handling: No change needed — the entry quotes an actual post-ask reply and names the channel (SendMessage), which is what this skill requires. The skill explicitly does NOT require an agent-bus citation — it states the bus only carries lifecycle events (dispatched/completed/errored/idle), not Q&A exchanges, and that this bar is reviewer-diligence, not tooling-enforced.
answer_key.distinguishes_A_from_B: Control case — both A and B must accept this as valid. A regression here (B rejecting a real, well-cited reply, or B wrongly demanding a bus-log citation the infrastructure can't provide) would be promotion-blocking.

scenarios.title: Bare confirmation claim with no quote and no channel
scenarios.context: Lane's autonomy-policy for this decision is `ask`. The lane's handoff receipt `## evidence` section reads only: "Orchestrator confirmed, proceeding with retry-with-backoff." No quoted reply, no channel named.
scenarios.question: Per this skill's '## Ask-gate semantics' section, is this entry sufficient? How should a reviewer treat it?

answer_key.required_handling: No quote, no channel — neither of the two required elements is present. Record as an `## assumptions` entry (audit only) and keep the gate closed.
answer_key.distinguishes_A_from_B: A has no explicit checklist of required elements, so a reader has to reconstruct why this fails from the general 'verbatim answer' instruction. B states the quote+channel bar directly, making the same conclusion reachable without inference.

scenarios.title: autonomy=all lane — no ask-gate directive expected at all
scenarios.context: Lane's resolved autonomy is `all` (`--auto-approve=all` / `defaults.auto_approve: all`). The assembled bundle for this lane does not embed the '## Ask-gate semantics' standing directive at all, per the section's own 'Omit this directive when...' rule. The lane's handoff receipt makes no confirmation-related claim in `## evidence` or `## assumptions`.
scenarios.question: Does the confirmation-provenance rule added in this edit apply to this lane's bundle or receipt?

answer_key.required_handling: Nothing to record; the bundle correctly omits the ask-gate directive under autonomy=all, and the new provenance rule (which only elaborates that directive) never triggers. This is distinct from the ask-gated case: an autonomy=all lane may make its own judgment calls without ever having asked in the first place — it never enters the `ask` branch this rule lives in.
answer_key.distinguishes_A_from_B: Both A and B must agree: no directive embedded, no behavior change. This is the no-change control confirming the edit is additive only inside the `autonomy=ask` branch and does not leak into the `autonomy=all` path.
